screening.proposed_ambiguous_instruction: I want to order a replacement for one of my chopping boards. Find a single board with the same visible shape and colour, not a set, and add it to the cart. Brand and size do not matter.
screening.continuous_review_method: Reviewed the complete local 180–202 second source interval using sequential full-resolution frames, with 0.2-second sampling over 187.0–192.4 seconds and exact timestamp checks.
screening.ambiguity_review: The request specifies a particular board to replace but leaves which board unspecified. It does not refer to the board being held, selected, most recently used, or taken out. Handling the white board is therefore not evidence of the authored replacement intent. Either pictured chopping board remains a possible intended reference until the fixed position answer.

supported_claims.text: The kitchen contains a white rectangular board with a rounded hand hole and a brown rectangular wood-grain board standing by the hob.
The white board lies flat on the counter; the brown board stands upright against the wall.
The fixed answer identifies the board by its flat position on the counter. Neither the initial request nor that answer names its colour, brand, size, or a website product.

construct.research_question: Can the agent resolve which kitchen chopping board the user wants to replace by asking one position question, then match its visible form and colour to a native cart item?
construct.belief_before: The standing brown board and the white board subsequently laid flat are both possible intended replacement references; activity alone does not declare which one the user wants to replace.
construct.belief_after: The fixed position answer identifies the board lying flat on the counter; visual evidence supplies its white rectangular form and rounded hand hole.
construct.required_behavior_change: Ask one position question before committing a product, then add exactly one accepted single-board listing matching the clarified physical board.
construct.no_update_failure: Choosing either board without clarification leaves the requested physical referent unresolved.
construct.overupdate_failure: Adding a product for both boards or buying a set violates the request for one replacement board.
construct.visual_dependency_claim: The position answer supplies only a physical location. Released frames are needed to connect that location to the board's white rectangular appearance and hand hole, while public product evidence supplies the purchasable equivalents.

task_blueprint.ambiguous_instruction: I want to order a replacement for one of my chopping boards. Find a single board with the same visible shape and colour, not a set, and add it to the cart. Brand and size do not matter.
task_blueprint.oracle_instruction: I want to order a replacement for the chopping board lying flat on the counter. Find a single board with the same visible shape and colour, not a set, and add it to the cart. Brand and size do not matter.
task_blueprint.canonical_question: Which chopping board do you mean?
task_blueprint.canonical_answer: The one lying flat on the counter.

observed.why: The one fixed position answer identifies the board lying flat on the counter. The frames establish its appearance; they do not establish the user's unstated replacement intent.

decision.note: Both physical roles are bound to real catalog entities at visible shape-and-colour granularity, not exact brand, dimensions, material, or wood grain. All 87 unique search-card images were individually reviewed. The white-board branch contains the canonical entity and 17 equivalents, including white rectangular boards with an integrated hand hole even when they have a juice groove. The PDP-sourced full-resolution images for B0006OLBU8 and B00CDL6X3C additionally confirm their integrated hand holes. The complete two-query union is bound and its 69 non-answer entities are classified. The generic shared titles on B000W4VFJ4 and B0DXWZTLRP were repaired from canonical snapshots on 2026-09-14; the full task-level semantic review remains unresolved. This record is not yet web_mapped.
